historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah' mentions a Berber tribe called the Banu Hilal, who were a part of the larger Sanhaja confederacy. The Banu Hilal, under their leader Ibn Zareer, were given permission to migrate from their lands in present-day Algeria to Egypt around 1064 AD due to a drought. They eventually settled in the Nile Delta and founded the city of Silaam, which became a major trading hub between Egypt and the Mediterranean.
historical_references.context: Migration of Banu Hilal Berbers from Algeria to Egypt

historical_references.reference: Around 1517 AD, Silaam came under the control of the Ottoman Empire when it was conquered by Ottoman Admiral Sinan Pasha. During this period, Silaam became an important port city, contributing significantly to the Ottoman maritime trade.
historical_references.context: Ottoman conquest and establishment of Silaam as a major port city
